findings.title: Registration distinguishes 'User already exists' (enumeration); audit-trail writes fire-and-forget
verification: vitest run tests/security/register-bypass-isolation.test.ts -> 6/6 pass (updated to assert the new generic response + no cross-tenant leak + no duplicate created)
vitest run tests/security/wave1-audit-trail-criticality.test.ts -> 7/7 pass (destructive/role events rethrow; non-critical events log-and-swallow; success path silent)
vitest run tests/security/audit-trail-sensitive-actions.test.ts tests/security/auditTrail/hash-chain.test.ts -> 3/3, 5/5 pass (no regression)
tsc --noEmit -> exit 0; eslint on both changed source files -> 0 errors, only pre-existing any-warnings unrelated to the changed lines
findings.notes: VERIFIED (continuation session). Enumeration: app/api/auth/register/route.ts's existing-user branch no longer returns a distinct 'User already exists' 400 -- it responds with the same 2xx shape a fresh registration would (no duplicate account created either way; enforcement unchanged). Residual gap documented, not fully closed: the frontend's auto-login-then-redirect step still distinguishes existing (redirect /login on wrong password) from new (redirect /onboarding) accounts via behavior, not response text -- closing that fully requires a bigger product-flow change (e.g. email-verification-gated registration) out of this session's scope; logged as P2-60. Audit-trail: lib/observability/auditTrail.ts's recordAuditTrailEvent() already logged failures (logger.warn) and rethrew for stripe./session./apikey. events (pre-existing, re-verified) -- extended the critical-rethrow classification to also cover data.deletion_* (tenant deletion) and role.* (role/permission changes), so those destructive/security categories can no longer be silently swallowed by a call site's own .catch(() => {}). Single shared-boundary fix, not per-caller patches.

findings.title: Four ENABLE_*_AUDIT_MODULE feature flags mutable via admin API but read nowhere
verification: vitest run tests/security/feature-flag-effective-override.test.ts (5/5): DB override flips the effective value module gating sees; cache invalidation picks up a fresh admin write; unknown/stale DB keys fail safe (ignored, not injected); DB-unavailable falls back to static defaults instead of throwing

vitest run tests/architecture/canonical-module-manifest.test.ts (7/7): FEATURE_FLAG_GATED_MODULES only gates real canonical modules and matches each module's declared rolloutFlag exactly, in both directions
tsc --noEmit exit 0; eslint 0 errors
findings.notes: Two-part fix. (1) lib/audit/runner.ts's executePhase() now gates each flagged module inline (accessibility/coreWebVitals/seoDeep/security) via FEATURE_FLAG_GATED_MODULES + isFeatureEnabledEffective(), reporting a disabled module as SKIPPED/"DISABLED: <flag>" (distinct from a dependency-skip or provider failure). (2) A DEEPER, previously-undiscovered half of this defect found during Wave 2 verification: the admin API (app/api/admin/feature-flags/route.ts) persisted toggles to the FeatureFlag DB table, but the static, env-computed FEATURE_FLAGS object could never see that table -- so even after modules were wired to read a flag, an admin's runtime toggle still had zero actual effect on execution (only on the admin API's own read response). Added lib/config/feature-flags.ts::getEffectiveFeatureFlags()/isFeatureEnabledEffective() as the one shared DB-override-aware read path; both the admin route and the module gate now go through it (single selection layer, no second framework). All 4 flags default to enabled (opt-out only), preserving current behavior for operators who never touch the admin API.

findings.title: claraud-web NextAuth adapter/OAuth wired but no catch-all route mounts `handlers` -- Google OAuth unreachable; PrismaAdapter calls would fail closed if ever reached
verification: Confirmed via file listing: no claraud-web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts exists
findings.notes: Discovered while fixing P1-07/P1-18: PrismaAdapter(prisma) uses the tenant-scoped client; its internal Account/Session/User bookkeeping calls run with no tenant/bypass context. Currently inert because there is no HTTP route serving NextAuth's own endpoints (no [...nextauth]/route.ts), so Google OAuth cannot complete and the adapter is unreachable. If a future wave adds that route, adapter calls must be wrapped in an auth-adapter-style allowlisted bypass (mirroring the root app's lib/auth/adapterContext.ts) before OAuth is exercised, or they will throw 'Tenant context required' -- a safe failure, not a silent one, but still needs the missing route + bypass wiring to actually work.

findings.title: Registration enumeration only partially closed -- auto-login redirect target still distinguishes existing vs new accounts
verification: Manual trace of app/(auth)/register/page.tsx's handleSubmit: existing-email + guessed-password -> signIn fails -> redirect /login; new-email -> signIn always succeeds -> redirect /onboarding
findings.notes: P2-23 closed the direct response-text/status oracle (no more distinct 'User already exists' 400). The frontend's immediate auto-login-then-redirect step is a residual, harder-to-close side channel: an existing email with a wrong guessed password still observably redirects to /login instead of /onboarding, unlike a genuinely new email (which always redirects to /onboarding, since the account was just created with that exact password). Fully closing this requires a bigger, product-level flow change (e.g. always show a generic 'check your email' step instead of auto-login) that was judged out of scope for a blind same-session change; flagged for a future wave/product decision.
